text:
Laura Chen: Quick followup on the allocator RFC — brain-dumping a bounded compact-runner approach. TL;DR: an async background compact/merge worker that consumes a *bounded* budget (time/pages) per epoch to avoid tail-latency spikes while doing continuous defrag.
Dan O'Neill: Nice. Two quick Qs: how do we avoid compacting hot pages? and how do tenants opt out?
Laura Chen: Good calls. Idea: compact-runner only targets pages with a low hotness score (sampled) and respects a per-tenant "compact_budget" token. If tenant has high latency SLO, allocator marks its pages as low-priority.
Mike K: How do we compute hotness cheaply? per-page counters will be heavy.
Sara Patel: Sampling + decay worked well in other systems. Maintain a tiny exponential moving average sampled on accesses (~1% sampling). That and a bloom-ish hotset filter. Cheap and amortized.
Laura Chen: Sketch of the API I had in mind:
```
// alloc returns a handle; flags include compact_priority and pin_hint
alloc(size, flags={
  "compact_priority": "low|normal|high",
  "pin_hint": "hot|cold|unknown"
}) -> alloc_handle

// runner polls pages and uses sample heatmap. bounded by time_ms or pages_per_epoch
start_compact_runner(budget_ms=100, pages_limit=1024)
```
Mike K: I like typed hints. Concern: adding flags to hot codepaths increases CPU overhead. We should keep flags metadata off the hot path: store compact_priority in the allocation descriptor (already in metadata) and read it only from runner.
Rohan Singh: Cross-node/page-migration cost: if we compact by migrating pages between pools we might pay PCIe/NVMe cost. The runner must estimate migration cost and prefer in-place compaction (coalesce free space) first.
Laura Chen: Agreed. Runner policy order: 1) in-place reclamation/coalesce, 2) local pool shuffle, 3) remote migration (only if benefit > threshold). The threshold is a simple cost model: cost_move < expected_latency_savings * weight.
Sara Patel: Also propose a small defrag epoch backoff if we detect recent latency spikes. E.g. double the budget window when 95th latency > target.
Dan O'Neill: What about correctness during compaction? need quiesce points or copy-on-write semantics for pinned ranges.
Laura Chen: We'll use per-page migration state + sequence numbers so in-flight kernels check a page token. If pinned, runner skips. That avoids global quiesce.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for branch "bounded-compact" on lab-cluster-3 (no traffic) :rocket:
Mike K: For rollout plan: start with budget_ms=50, pages_limit=256; perf-run with embedding-heavy workloads and tiny-batch chat. Measure p95 token latency and fragmentation histogram.
Rohan Singh: One more edge: memory accounting race when runner frees a page and allocator races to reuse it. Suggest an ephemeral retire-list where pages are retired for a single epoch before reuse to avoid races.
Laura Chen: Good safety belt. I'll prototype retire-list + sample-based heatmap. Volunteer to own the prototype; will open RFC PR and perf script. Anyone want to pair on the perf harness?
Sara Patel: I'll help with sampling impl and instrumentation.
Dan O'Neill: Happy to run the perf harness and check SLO impact.
Laura Chen: Thanks all. I'll push a design note later with a small diagram and the cost model. For now, next steps: prototype, perf, and iterate. :thumbsup:
